newsitem.title: HONDURAS: North and Central America port conditions - Lloyds.
newsitem.headline: North and Central America port conditions - Lloyds.

text.p: Port conditions from Lloyds Shipping Intelligence Service --

HONDURAS, June 2 - Puerto Cortes - four vessels berthed of which 2 discharging/loading containers/general, 1 discharging fertiliser, 1 loading lumber. 24 due of which 1 passenger, 12 to discharge/load containers/general, 6 to discharge/load containers/bananas, 1 each to discharge generals, vehicles, liquid chemicals, fuel oil, 1 to load lumber.

MEXICO, June 3 - Tampico - vessels in port - 1 container, 1 grain, 1 lead, 1 pipes, 2 steel coils, 1 clinker, 1 corn, 1 asphalt, 2 minerals. working normally. Altamira - vessels in port - 1 container, 1 general cargo, 1 steel coils, 1 chemical, 1 repairs. Working normally. Veracruz - vessels in port - 3 containers, 2 sugar, 4 corn, 3 grain, 1 pipes, 1 fish oil, 1 repairs, 1 chemical. working normally. Manzanillo - vessels in port - 2 containers, 3 general cargo, 2 cars, 1 milk powder, 1 steel coils, 1 cement. Working normally. Coatzacoalcos - vessels in port - 9 chemicals, 5 oil tankers, 1 repairs. Working normally.
PANAMA, June 2 - Cristobal, Balboa - working normally.
PANAMA CANAL - Waterway operating to full capacity. Thirty-two vessels due. 17 in queue, 9 booked, 29 scheduled.

UNITED STATES, June 2 - Port Newark, Bayway, Cartaret, nj - One vessel in each port. Port Elizabeth, Perth Amboy - two vessels in each port. Hampton Roads, va - six general cargo/container vessels in PIER operating, 3 bulkers loading coal in pier, 2 bulkers loading fertiliser, 1 bulker discharging cement, 2 vessels in pier under layberth arrangement.

Baltimore, md - vessels operating - 8 bulkers, 2 Container vessels, 3 ro/ro, 2 auto vessels, 1 tanker, 3 general cargo, 2 cable vessels on stand, 2 vessels in repair yard, 2 bulkers awaiting berth of which 1 to discharge sugar, 1 to discharge ore.

East coast - Baltimore, md - no congestion at Dundalk terminal anticipated this week. Elevator and coal operations working well with no delays. Average waiting time, Consol coal 4 days. Liquid bulk facilities operating normally, no berthing congestion. Anchorage available at Baltimore and Annapolis.

Charleston, sc - the SC Port Authority is continuing to dredge along the Columbus Street terminal. Vessel movement has not been affected by the work and no delays are expected. The oil facilities in Charleston report moderate vessel activity for next week, while there are no vessels scheduled at the grain terminal. No conditions are expected which will delay vessel movement or cargo operations. Hurricane season starts 1 June.

Jacksonville - no heavy berth congestion or delays for the ports of Jacksonville and Fernandina Peach, fl. Mmi, fl - traffic is expected to be normal this week at both ports, Miami and Everglades. However, lots of rain is forecast. Passenger terminals are available From Tuesday to Thursday. From Friday 0600 hrs to Monday 1900 hrs these terminals are fully operational.

New york, ny - no congestion in New York anchorage, tanker terminals. No congestion in sugar terminals. Norfolk, va - Norfolk southern coal pier expecting 8 vessels during this week. Dominion terminal is expecting 3 vessels. Pier IX terminal is expecting 3 vessels during the next week. Norfolk Southern coal pier 6 will, effective June 1, 1997, increase the cost of vessel docking, shifting and undocking (all services). Cargill is not expecting any vessels during the coming week. Container and general cargo terminals are working normally with no delays. Oil and bulk terminals are all working normally. All channels are opening, with prevailing depths available.

Philadelphia, pa - There is no port congestion at the ports of Philadelphia, Camden, Wilmington. No activity as far as dredging/repairs/navigational problems. Gulf Coast - Houston, tx - the port of Houston is congested for vessels requiring open docks. This will last until next week. Congestion also exists in some oil/chemical terminals and private terminals for breakbulk cargo such as Greensport and Manchester. No Congestion at farmland grain elevator, Cargill grain elevator and Houston public grain elevator.

New Orleans, la - it is normal for periods of rain to occur during summer season and these conditions cause delays in cargo operation especially grain loading. Grain shipments normal for this season. River stage at 8.2 feet. Expect to go down to 8.1 ft. Normal transit times can be expected.

Bar pilots advise that the draft for the Mississippi River Gulf outlet will be 36 ft. Based on these drafts, all vessels to maintain sufficient Aircraft for transit under bridges in Mississippi river.

High river conditions will cause delays in ship movement and vessel transit times. Present max permissible draft at S.W. pass is 45 ft fresh water for vessels under 100,000 dwt, 44 ft fresh water for vessels over 100,000 dwt.

Some elevators are not working weekends due to slower than usual grain shipments. Zennoh Grain Convent Managements advise repairs to their elevator will take several months but engineers cannot establish a more exact time frame for resuming normal operations. Indications are the elevator will be ready for loading August 1997.

West Coast - Columbia River - high water conditions continue to slow vessel transits and in certain cases bulk loading productions due to vessels sitting too high in the water to place loading spouts into cargo holds.

Grain activity increasing due to current Pakistan cargo tenders taking place in May/June. Average waiting period for grain elevators is 2-4 days. Coos Bay - past week normal. Port has slowed down from the rapid fire vessels arrivals and departures of the previous week. Only one vessel discharging nickel ore at Glenbrook terminal and one vessel loading woodchips at Roseburg dock. Schedule for the coming week picks up with four vessels due to arrive/two woodchip carriers, one lumber vessel and one log vessel.

Honolulu, hi - over 400 longshoremen from both of Hawaii's stevedore companies walked off the job this week in protest over a labour dispute with a metal recycling firm. The Dispute is still ongoing, however, a federal judge ordered the Stevedores back to work. The walk out has caused delays of 2 days for vessels in Barber's Point harbour and 1 day in Honolulu harbour. A New tractor tug will be delivered to Smith Maritime in Honolulu next Week. It is expected to work in inter-island towing and perform some ship assist work.

Long Beach, Los Angeles - no congestion at bulk/other terminals reported/expected. San Francisco, ca - the ports of Stockton and Sacramento are still under reduced transit draft restrictions. The anchorages are clear, however, the weather has been unpredictable. Fog is a possibility for vessels coming from sea. Seattle - Puget sound ports are slow with little waiting time for the Grain elevators, log or chip docks.
